requirement: Implement an Anthropic message streaming handler that safely manages stream context lifecycle, records text chunks, detects token limit truncation, and handles stream errors.
skeleton: AnthropicStreamHandler with collect_stream and stream_text_chunks methods returning StreamSummary dataclass.

rationale.teaches: Streaming through the messages.stream context manager, reading the final message inside it, flagging max_tokens as truncation, refusing empty messages, and defaulting max_tokens to 1024.
rationale.why: A stream used outside its context manager still yields text, but its connection is never closed. The fixture uses a fake stream that records enter and exit and reports stop_reason.

candidates.why_wrong: The stream is used outside its context manager, so the connection is never closed after the final message.
end_turn is flagged as truncation, so every normal completion is reported as truncated and real truncation is not.
Empty message lists are sent to the API, so the error surfaces from the client instead of as a ValueError.
max_tokens defaults to 100, so a normal response is truncated by default.
get_final_message is called after leaving the context, so the stop reason is read from a closed stream.
